articles.title: Democrats in Maine gather to replace Graham Platner in the race against Susan Collins
articles.summary: Democrats are hoping to move past Platner's scandal-plagued campaign as they look to unseat Republican incumbent Susan Collins. The apparent front-runner is former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson.
articles.titleZh: 缅因州的民主党人聚集在一起，在与苏珊·柯林斯的竞选中取代格雷厄姆·普拉特纳
articles.summaryZh: 民主党人希望摆脱普拉特纳丑闻缠身的竞选活动，希望推翻共和党现任议员苏珊·柯林斯(Susan Collins)。明显的领先者是前缅因州参议院主席特洛伊·杰克逊。

contentParagraphs.en: Maine Democrats will gather Saturday to name a new nominee in the race for U.S. Senate. Former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson is seen as the front-runner. Above, Jackson speaks at a rally organized by local unions on May 1 in Portland, Maine.
contentParagraphs.zh: 缅因州民主党人将于周六齐聚一堂，提名美国参议院竞选的新提名人。前缅因州参议院议长特洛伊·杰克逊被视为领先者。上图是杰克逊 5 月 1 日在缅因州波特兰当地工会组织的集会上发表的讲话。

contentParagraphs.en: Democrats are gathering in Bangor, Maine, on Saturday to formally nominate a new candidate for U.S. Senate, as the party looks to move past the scandal-plagued campaign of Graham Platner and refocus its sights on unseating longtime Republican incumbent Susan Collins.
contentParagraphs.zh: 民主党人周六聚集在缅因州班戈，正式提名美国参议院的新候选人，该党希望摆脱格雷厄姆·普拉特纳丑闻缠身的竞选活动，重新把目光集中在推翻长期共和党现任议员苏珊·柯林斯身上。

contentParagraphs.en: It's a Senate matchup with far-reaching political implications. Democrats need to net a total of four seats to win back control of the chamber this fall, and party officials see the contest in Maine as one of their best opportunities.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这是一场具有深远政治影响的参议院对决。民主党需要在今年秋天赢得总共四个席位才能重新赢得众议院的控制权，党的官员认为缅因州的竞选是他们最好的机会之一。

contentParagraphs.en: The race was thrown into turmoil earlier this month when Platner, the party's initial nominee, ended his campaign after a woman he previously dated came forward and accused him of raping her in 2021. Platner has denied the allegation, but it was the final straw for Democrats after months of controversy surrounding him.
contentParagraphs.zh: 本月早些时候，该党最初的提名人普拉特纳结束了竞选活动，原因是他之前约会过的一名女子站出来指控他在 2021 年强奸了她。普拉特纳否认了这一指控，但这成为压垮民主党的最后一根稻草。

contentParagraphs.en: Now, after an abbreviated and chaotic search for a replacement, Maine Democrats are hoping to rally behind a new candidate who can harness the same energy and momentum of the Platner campaign.
contentParagraphs.zh: 现在，在短暂而混乱地寻找替代者之后，缅因州民主党人希望团结起来支持一位新候选人，他可以利用与普拉特纳竞选活动相同的能量和势头。

contentParagraphs.en: The apparent front-runner heading into Saturday's convention is Troy Jackson. The former president of the Maine Senate has already garnered support from the bulk of elected delegates who will cast ballots for the nominee, and nearly every one of his primary rivals has dropped out of the race.
contentParagraphs.zh: 参加周六大会的明显领跑者是特洛伊·杰克逊。这位缅因州参议院前议长已经获得了将为提名人投票的大部分当选代表的支持，而他的几乎所有主要竞争对手都退出了竞选。

contentParagraphs.en: Maintaining Platner's movement, without the baggage
contentParagraphs.zh: 在没有行李的情况下保持普拉特纳的运动

contentParagraphs.en: Jackson, a fifth-generation logger from northern Maine, is running on an economic populist message that mirrors much of what Platner emphasized in his campaign, rejecting the Democratic establishment and focusing on affordability concerns, backing policies like Medicare for All and raising taxes on the ultra-wealthy and large corporations.
contentParagraphs.zh: 杰克逊是来自缅因州北部的第五代伐木工，他所传达的经济民粹主义信息与普拉特纳在竞选中强调的大部分内容相呼应，拒绝民主党建制派，关注负担能力问题，支持全民医疗保险等政策，并提高对超级富豪和大公司的税收。

contentParagraphs.en: Like other more progressive candidates on the left, Jackson is pushing for the abolishment of Immigration and Customs Enforcement and an end to U.S. military aid to Israel. He's also advocating for Congress to pass civil rights legislation protecting LGBTQ Americans and federalize the right to an abortion — two issues where he's changed his views after taking more conservative stances during his early years in public office.
contentParagraphs.zh: 与其他更进步的左翼候选人一样，杰克逊正在推动废除移民和海关执法以及结束美国对以色列的军事援助。他还主张国会通过保护 LGBTQ 美国人的民权立法，并将堕胎权联邦化——在担任公职初期采取更加保守的立场后，他在这两个问题上改变了看法。

contentParagraphs.en: When asked about Jackson's history with reproductive rights, Democratic state Sen. Stacy Brenner argued that it wasn't a deterrent in supporting him.
contentParagraphs.zh: 当被问及杰克逊在生育权方面的历史时，民主党州参议员史黛西·布伦纳 (Stacy Brenner) 辩称，这并不妨碍支持他。

contentParagraphs.en: "What I find compelling about legislators and policymakers is when they are able to evolve with the thinking of where their heart is, where their mind is, when they learn about data and when they hear stories [from] their constituents," said Brenner, who also has a background as a farmer and nurse.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我发现立法者和政策制定者的吸引力在于，当他们了解数据以及听到选民的故事时，他们能够思考自己的心在哪里，他们的思想在哪里，从而不断发展，”布伦纳说，他也有农民和护士的背景。

contentParagraphs.en: "That's what's happened for Troy," she added.
contentParagraphs.zh: “这就是特洛伊发生的事情，”她补充道。

contentParagraphs.en: Jackson supporters celebrate his lengthy tenure in Maine politics as well as his blue-collar roots. And despite recent reporting in The Washington Post and CNN describing Jackson as exhibiting a short temper with colleagues during his time in office, he has faced minimal public pushback from state leaders in the lead-up to the convention.
contentParagraphs.zh: 杰克逊的支持者庆祝他在缅因州政坛的长期任期以及他的蓝领出身。尽管《华盛顿邮报》和美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 最近的报道称杰克逊在任职期间对同事表现出脾气暴躁，但在大会召开之前，他受到的州领导人的公开阻力微乎其微。

contentParagraphs.en: A tough road ahead for the nominee
contentParagraphs.zh: 被提名者的前路艰难

contentParagraphs.en: While Collins has faced competitive challengers before, Democrats see the fifth-term incumbent as particularly vulnerable this year. She's running in a state carried by Kamala Harris in 2024, and at a moment when many voters have soured on President Trump's handling of the economy and the war in Iran.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管柯林斯之前曾面临过竞争性挑战者，但民主党人认为这位第五任总统今年特别容易受到攻击。 2024 年，她在卡马拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris) 领导的州竞选，而此时许多选民对特朗普总统对经济和伊朗战争的处理方式感到不满。

contentParagraphs.en: Still, even if Jackson is able to claim the nomination, he will face a difficult path to victory, with only about 100 days before voting ends on Nov. 3 to build up a war chest and make his case to voters.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管如此，即使杰克逊能够获得提名，他也将面临一条艰难的胜利之路，距离11月3日投票结束只有大约100天的时间来筹集资金并向选民证明他的观点。

contentParagraphs.en: In Collins, he would be facing off against one of the most senior Republican incumbents in the Senate. Collins, who has held her seat for 30 years, holds a massive fundraising edge, reporting $11 million in cash on hand, according to latest Federal Election Commission filings.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在柯林斯，他将面对参议院最资深的共和党现任议员之一。根据联邦选举委员会最新提交的文件，柯林斯已担任该席位 30 年，拥有巨大的筹款优势，手头现金为 1100 万美元。

contentParagraphs.en: Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, walks in the annual Moxie Day Parade on July 11 in Lisbon, Maine.
contentParagraphs.zh: 7 月 11 日，缅因州共和党参议员苏珊·柯林斯 (Susan Collins) 参加在缅因州里斯本举行的一年一度的莫克西日游行。

contentParagraphs.en: But Jackson's campaign argues that it has momentum, reporting a fundraising haul of more than $1 million since he announced his run.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但杰克逊的竞选活动称其势头强劲，据报道自他宣布参选以来筹款额已超过 100 万美元。

contentParagraphs.en: "This campaign is powered by people who are sick of watching billionaires and corporations buy influence while working families get screwed," Jackson said in a statement Wednesday.
contentParagraphs.zh: 杰克逊在周三的一份声明中表示，“这场运动的发起者是那些厌倦了看着亿万富翁和企业收买影响力而工薪家庭受骗的人。”

contentParagraphs.en: "Together, we're building the grassroots movement it will take to defeat Susan Collins and give Maine a senator who answers to working people."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们正在共同开展草根运动，以击败苏珊·柯林斯，并为缅因州提供一位对劳动人民负责的参议员。”

articles.summaryZh:
阿夫塔花了几十年的时间想知道他从未认识的母亲发生了什么事。千里之外，尼奇的同父异母兄弟在她出生前被送走的故事一直困扰着她。聊天机器人是如何将他们聚集在一起的？
作为一个在印度阿姆利则长大的小男孩，19世纪

contentParagraphs.en: As a small boy growing up in Amritsar, India, in the 1960s, Avtar Singh used to hear whispers. Your mum isn’t really your mum, the rumours would say. Your mum lives abroad. Avtar didn’t really pay any attention to it. “I thought, the neighbours are just making up stories.” But the stories were true: the woman raising Avtar was actually his grandmother. When he was too young to remember it, his father had emigrated to Canada to work as a teacher, leaving Avtar in the care of his paternal grandparents. His grandfather, a police officer, was a fearsome authoritarian, but his grandmother brought him up with tenderness, as if he were her own son. She called him by his nickname, Titu. He felt loved.When Avtar was around eight years old, he was told about his family in Canada: his dad, his mum and a little brother were waiting for him there, and he would soon travel to join them. Just after his ninth birthday, Avtar found himself sitting on a plane, dressed in a three‑piece suit and tie. He was travelling alone. He had never flown before. He didn’t speak a word of English. He landed in Halifax, Nova Scotia, on Christmas Eve, 1968; his family met him at the airport and took him home. “I didn’t know what to think,” Avtar, now 66, tells me in a video call from his home in Abbotsford, British Columbia. “Before I knew it, it was the first week of January, and I was put in school.”Avtar with his grandmother in the mid-60s in Amritsar, India (above), and (below) aged 10, in 1969, the year after he moved to Canada. Courtesy of Avtar SinghUnable to communicate with any of the other pupils, Avtar watched what they did and followed along, storing his snow boots in the cloakroom, standing up to sing the Canadian national anthem and God Save the Queen. But with his long hair tied in the topknot often worn by Sikh boys, he stood out. His parents offered to buy him a hockey stick and a pair of ice skates if he agreed to get his hair cut. He learned English. His nickname changed from Titu to the more Canadian “Tito”. He began to blend in.But Avtar didn’t fit in at home. He was much paler than everyone else – “the white sheep of the family,” he jokes. And they treated him like an outsider, an afterthought. When he was 14, his family went on holiday without him, leaving Avtar home alone for two weeks. He got on well enough with his father, but didn’t gel at all with his mother. “She didn’t have any of the warmth that my grandma had. She absolutely hated me.” She seemed much more like a stepmother than a mother.That feeling was confirmed when Avtar got married and his grandparents flew over to stay with him and his new wife, Rosie. His grandma “whispered into my wife’s ear” that Avtar was the product of his father’s first marriage. “She didn’t say what my mother’s name was. She just said, ‘Her family was from Africa, and she left the child with us and went back to Africa. She might have gone to live in the UK.’ That’s it.” It didn’t feel right to ask his grandparents for more information: this was clearly a family secret that no one wanted to discuss with Avtar.When his son was set a school assignment to complete his family tree, Avtar felt emboldened to approach his father. “I said, ‘Dad, you’ve got to tell me at least what my mother’s name was.’” His dad eventually relented: her first name was Savinder. But he would not give Avtar any more information, no matter how many times he asked. “I was stonewalled.” Avtar had no idea why his parents had split up. “All I really understood was that my mother’s family encouraged her to give up custody of me so it would be easier for them to remarry her.”He thought about his mother constantly. When Rosie was pregnant with their daughter, there were anomalies in some of the antenatal tests, and Rosie and Avtar were referred to a geneticist. Avtar was asked about his parents’ medical history. “I couldn’t tell them anything about my mother’s family history. It hit me right in the heart. That’s when I thought, I’ve got to do something.”He Googled and Facebooked, but there was almost nothing to go on; Savinder is a fairly common Punjabi Sikh name. In 2009, Avtar flew to London to visit the National Archives at Kew with the hope of finding immigration or marriage records that might lead him to his mother. “I couldn’t find anything at all.” On a later visit to London, he emailed Sunrise Radio, a British Asian station, asking if they could put out an appeal to find his mother, but they told Avtar they don’t do that kind of thing, out of respect for people’s privacy. That gave Avtar pause. “I thought, maybe I should just cool off. If my mother has some other family, I don’t want to disrupt her life.” Still, it niggled. Three or four years ago, he asked a British south Asian work colleague for advice; she suggested contacting the ITV show Long Lost Family. He watched a few episodes and decided it wasn’t for him. But he longed to know his mother. “The thought of her did not leave my mind, ever.”The one thing Avtar did not do was a DNA test. He is retired now, but he used to be a chartered accountant, and he knows enough about technology, data and privacy to be wary of giving up his genetic code to a corporation. “They can sell it. Not only that – if they see something in my DNA, that affects my kids. I don’t want that information up there.” He deactivated his Facebook account 12 years ago for similar reasons. “I don’t have faith that these companies have the proper safeguards.”Then, on 8 May this year, Avtar and Rosie were on holiday in the south of France. Avtar had been battling cancer; their long-awaited trip to Europe came after he had finished his treatment. “It was early morning, and I had read all the news. I was bored. I had nothing else to do. I thought, I’ve tried Google and everything else, why don’t I give AI a shot?”Savinder Kaur in 1963. articles.title: Long overdue, life-changing or frivolous? Your thoughts on wedding rule changes
articles.summary: The government wants to relax wedding laws so couples can get married almost anywhere.
articles.titleZh: 姗姗来迟、改变生活还是无聊？您对婚礼规则变化的看法
articles.summaryZh: 政府希望放宽婚礼法，以便情侣几乎可以在任何地方结婚。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, KJA Photography/Kimberley AppletonImage caption, Courtney and Sam Scholey had their dream wedding day at a venue in the Oxfordshire countryside - only it wasn't legalByTiffanie TurnbullThe day Sam and Courtney Scholey became husband and wife didn't feel like their wedding day.There was no walking down the aisle, no rings exchanged, no wedding dress, and no music.That all came several days later, when the pair had a bespoke ceremony led by a celebrant who knew them, at a venue in the Oxfordshire countryside. It was their dream wedding - but it wasn't legal in England and Wales.And so in April, they forked out hundreds of pounds to quietly sign papers at a library in Buckingham."For us, that day was as insignificant as possible," Courtney told the BBC. "It was just the words we had to say to make it legally binding."The Scholeys are one of a growing number of couples who feel the rigid rules around weddings are making getting married more stressful, more expensive and less meaningful.But under new proposals announced this month - described by the government as the biggest shake-up of wedding laws in 200 years - couples in England and Wales could have the freedom to hold official marriage ceremonies in a wider array of unconventional locations, from forests to beaches, as long as the location is approved by a registered officiant.It's welcome news for Nicky Brown, who said she wants to exchange vows in a wildly picturesque corner of Wales, with just her mum and her partner's mum as witnesses. "I'd be quite happy to get married in a field full of sheep," the 57-year-old told the BBC.But some say the sacred tradition of marriage is being perverted.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Wedding rules date back to the 18th and 19th CenturiesCurrently, a marriage or civil partnership ceremony in England or Wales must take place at an approved venue to be legally binding – and many exert control on elements of the wedding such as vows, headcounts or music.There are also tight restrictions on who can officiate a wedding and how. Authorised religious figures can, but – with few exceptions – only in places of worship. Registrars can conduct a wedding, but it can't have any religious content. And celebrants can't legally marry people at all.A Law Commission report in 2022 concluded that these marriage laws, which date back to the 18th and 19th Centuries, were "complicated, inefficient, unfair and needlessly restrictive".David Lammy, then deputy prime minister, said marriage laws in England and Wales had "not kept pace with the social and cultural changes that have shaped modern Britain".He added: "Some feel forced to pay for two different ceremonies, one legal and one belief based. Some enter into a marriage that isn't legally recognised. Others feel they have little choice but to marry in a way which doesn't reflect their beliefs, marring what should be a joyous occasion."Scotland and Northern Ireland relaxed their rules years ago. Though the exact shape of the new rules is still under public consultation until September, these changes will take regulations from a "buildings based" regulation model to an "officiant based" one.'The laws are now, what, 200 years out of date?'Brown said she and her partner had put off getting married because there was no legal and affordable version of a wedding that reflects them.She said she didn't want bells and whistles - or even a wedding dress. "I just want somebody to marry us and in a beautiful setting that isn't just going to cost the earth."Brown went on to explain that she'd been scared her mum - who is 86 and unwell - would miss out on her wedding day. But these proposals had given her hope: "The laws are now, what, 200 years out of date?"Miranda Allard, 66, agreed that change is long overdue.When she got married 40 years ago, she had to jump through hoops to get permission to hold an interfaith ceremony in her parent's garden - and finds it astounding couples today face the same obstacles."We applied for a special licence... [and] explained how we did not want to put my Jewish mother-in-law through a church wedding," she said."I, on the other hand, was brought up in a Christian family and would not 'feel married' if doing so in a registry office."It took letters from the couple, their parents, the local bishop, the village vicar and more to convince authorities to allow the ceremony."We also combined our legal Christian service with Jewish prayers and tradition, like breaking the glass. Totally unheard of then and ever since," she said, adding the nuptials even made the paper.Image source, Miranda AllardImage caption, Simon and Miranda Allard had to get permission to hold an interfaith ceremony in her parent's garden when they got married 40 years ago... articles.title: It's the cocktail taking young drinkers by storm - but the packaging is 'unrecyclable'
articles.summary: BuzzBallz cannot be recycled because the metal lid and plastic body are attached, say experts.
articles.titleZh: 这款鸡尾酒风靡年轻饮酒者，但其包装“不可回收”
articles.summaryZh: 专家表示，BuzzBallz 无法回收，因为金属盖和塑料机身是相连的。

contentParagraphs.en: BuzzBallz was founded by teacher Merrilee Kick, but was bought by the Sazerac Company, whose CEO is Jake Wenz, in 2024.BuzzBallz's UK's mission statement, which was deleted after the BBC contacted the company about this story, said it "loves our planet as much as we love a good cocktail" and partnered with TerraCycle to ensure its packaging gets recycled. However, TerraCycle, which involves consumers collecting packaging and sending it to be recycled, only runs the BuzzBallz scheme in the United States. BuzzBallz's UK FAQs, now also deleted, stated: "Yes, our packaging is recyclable. Please recycle your empties where local facilities allow."But no local facilities anywhere in the UK allow BuzzBallz to be recycled, said Adam Herriott, the head of packaging at WRAP."They're a mix of two very recyclable materials that put together makes an unrecyclable format."No local authorities will accept these at the kerbside."If they end up at a sorting facility, they could end up contaminating the plastic stream because of the metals in there and that could be very problematic for plastics recyclers that get into the machinery."But why should people care if their drink packaging is not recyclable?Even the shape of the BuzzBallz make it harder to be recycled because they can roll on the conveyor belts at the sorting facilities, said Herriott. Among the machinery used, scanners can identify it in one position, but by the time air jets are used to separate it into the right recycling stream, it could have moved, meaning it could contaminate other streams. "It's definitely one of the villains of recycling," said Ambarish Mitra, co-founder of Greyparrot, a waste analytics company which helps recovery facilities. He said BuzzBallz have "have no recovery route in the current system" and "is a huge pet peeve for our customers and us".After analysing a plastic recover facility in Manchester with a processing capacity of 35,000 tonnes of plastic a year, for six months, the company found that BuzzBallz contaminated recycled plastic 66% of the time. "Once in the plastic stream, the aluminium reduces the quality of the recycled plastic, while the colour pigments can lower the recycled plastic bale's value."This isn't a recycling problem. It's a packaging problem."BuzzBallz refused to comment.James Piper, co-host of the Talking Rubbish podcast, co-owner of Ecosurety, said he dislikes BuzzBallz because of how difficult they are to recycle. "Every stage of the recycling journey has been designed around predictable packaging," Piper said. "When people come along and say, 'I'm going to make something different for marketing reasons', they are automatically making it more difficult for the recycler.""There's nothing environmentally positive about mixing packaging types."He said the BuzzBallz 'biggies' which have a plastic screw top lid is completely recyclable."Anyone can say on their website 'this is recyclable where your council allows'. But if no council allows it, then it doesn't mean anything," he said. BuzzBallz said: "We very recently went through a global website update and the information pertaining to TerraCycle recycling for BuzzBallz was incorrectly copied and does not apply to the UK market as of today. "We apologise for the oversight and have since updated our website to reflect the correct position for UK consumers."The company refused to comment on the now-deleted UK FAQs stating its packaging was recyclable.

articles.title: Trump is hellbent on tariffs. Here are 5 implications
articles.summary: Trump's determination to find new legal justifications for his tariffs threatens to prolong the uncertainty facing the U.S. and global economies.
articles.titleZh: 特朗普对关税一意孤行。这里有 5 个含义
articles.summaryZh: 特朗普决心为其关税寻找新的法律理由，这可能会延长美国和全球经济面临的不确定性。

contentParagraphs.en: Trump imposed a new set of sweeping tariffs this week, arguing they will benefit the U.S. economy — and American workers. But there is plenty of signs tariffs will end up hurting many households.
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普本周实施了一套新的全面关税，称这些关税将有利于美国经济和美国工人。但有大量迹象表明关税最终将损害许多家庭。

contentParagraphs.en: President Trump's second term has been marked by intense economic uncertainty, from the war with Iran to tensions with countries around the world – and there appears to be no reprieve coming.
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普总统的第二个任期充满了严重的经济不确定性，从与伊朗的战争到与世界各国的紧张关系，而且似乎不会有任何缓解。

contentParagraphs.en: The White House said on Thursday the U.S. would replace a temporary 10% tariff it had imposed earlier this year with a batch of new ones covering dozens of countries.
contentParagraphs.zh: 白宫周四表示，美国将取消今年早些时候征收的 10% 临时关税，并征收覆盖数十个国家的一批新关税。

contentParagraphs.en: The new levies, which kicked in on Friday after midnight, range from 10% to 12.5%, and they are meant to be more legally durable — though economists still say they are likely to be challenged.
contentParagraphs.zh: 新的税收于周五午夜后开始实施，税率从 10% 到 12.5% 不等，其目的是在法律上更加持久——尽管经济学家仍然表示它们可能会受到挑战。

contentParagraphs.en: Here are five takeaways as Trump remains fixated on tariffs.
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普仍然专注于关税，以下是五个要点。

contentParagraphs.en: 1. No immediate relief for American households
contentParagraphs.zh: 1.美国家庭不会立即得到缓解

contentParagraphs.en: It's already been a rough ride for many families, with the cost of living remaining a top concern after years of high inflation.
contentParagraphs.zh: 对于许多家庭来说，这已经是一段艰难的旅程，在多年的高通胀之后，生活成本仍然是首要问题。

contentParagraphs.en: Things may not get better anytime soon. The renewed tensions with Iran are threatening to push up gas prices and broader energy costs — raising the prospect that inflation could once again pick up after prices had finally seemed to ease in June.
contentParagraphs.zh: 情况可能不会很快好转。与伊朗的新一轮紧张局势有可能推高天然气价格和更广泛的能源成本——这增加了在六月份价格似乎最终回落后通胀可能再次上升的可能性。

contentParagraphs.en: The national average for gas prices is back up above $4 a gallon, according to AAA, after dipping below that level in late June as crude prices once again surge.
contentParagraphs.zh: AAA 表示，随着原油价格再次飙升，全国平均天然气价格在 6 月下旬跌破每加仑 4 美元后，已回升至每加仑 4 美元以上。

contentParagraphs.en: Meanwhile, the average 30-year mortgage rate this week hit its highest in nearly a year and remains historically high.
contentParagraphs.zh: 与此同时，本周30年期抵押贷款平均利率创下近一年来的最高水平，仍处于历史高位。

contentParagraphs.en: Now Trump's determination to find new legal ways to justify tariffs on imported goods threaten to burden households for longer.
contentParagraphs.zh: 现在，特朗普决心寻找新的合法途径来证明对进口商品征收关税的合理性，这可能会给家庭带来更长时间的负担。

contentParagraphs.en: The new tariffs are not significantly higher than the ones they are replacing, and there are carveouts in place.
contentParagraphs.zh: 新的关税并没有明显高于他们所取代的关税，而且还存在一些例外情况。

contentParagraphs.en: But they are still higher than when Trump's second term started, with a current average rate of 11%, according to the Budget Lab at Yale University.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但根据耶鲁大学预算实验室的数据，这一数字仍高于特朗普第二任期开始时的水平，目前平均率为 11%。

contentParagraphs.en: The prospect of continued tariffs could extend the financial burden on Americans – imposing an additional cost of about $1,100 on households, according to Budget Lab.
contentParagraphs.zh: 预算实验室表示，持续征收关税的前景可能会增加美国人的经济负担——给家庭带来约 1,100 美元的额外成本。

contentParagraphs.en: 2. The path to lower interest rates is tougher
contentParagraphs.zh: 2.降低利率的道路更加艰难

contentParagraphs.en: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh inherited a challenging job when he was sworn in back in May.
contentParagraphs.zh: 新任美联储主席凯文·沃什 (Kevin Warsh) 在五月份宣誓就职时继承了一项充满挑战的工作。

contentParagraphs.en: Inflation remains a top concern for policy makers even though the U.S. economy has been relatively stable recently.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管美国经济近期相对稳定，但通胀仍然是政策制定者最关心的问题。

contentParagraphs.en: If inflation starts to rise, the Fed may need to raise rates – in a rebuke to President Trump who appointed Warsh hoping the central bank would be more willing to cut rates instead.
contentParagraphs.zh: 如果通胀开始上升，美联储可能需要加息——这是对特朗普总统的谴责，特朗普总统任命沃什希望美联储更愿意降息。

contentParagraphs.en: Trump's determination to extend his tariffs – and his administration's threat to impose additional ones – will keep additional economic uncertainty in place
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普延长关税的决心 — — 以及他的政府威胁征收更多关税 — — 将带来额外的经济不确定性

contentParagraphs.en: "If there are tariffs imposed and if they stick, that is certainly going to drive up the prices of imports, which is going to add to inflation," says Eswar Prasad, a professor at Cornell University.
contentParagraphs.zh: 康奈尔大学教授埃斯瓦尔·普拉萨德表示：“如果征收关税并且坚持下去，肯定会推高进口产品价格，从而加剧通货膨胀。”

contentParagraphs.en: 3. More uncertainty for businesses that rely on imports
contentParagraphs.zh: 3. 依赖进口的企业面临更多不确定性

contentParagraphs.en: Ever since Trump imposed his initial set of tariffs last year, businesses have faced a period of intense volatility.
contentParagraphs.zh: 自从特朗普去年实施最初的一系列关税以来，企业面临着一段剧烈波动的时期。

contentParagraphs.en: Business owners were able to get some reprieve after the Supreme Court struck down many of Trump's tariffs – allowing many to get refunds from the import taxes they had already paid.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在最高法院推翻特朗普的许多关税后，企业主得以获得一些缓刑——允许许多人从他们已经缴纳的进口税中获得退款。

contentParagraphs.en: But Trump's determination to continue to impose tariffs threaten to prolong the uncertainty. The president responded to the Supreme Court setback with a temporary 10% tariff, drawing fresh legal challenges.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但特朗普继续征收关税的决心可能会延长不确定性。总统以临时征收 10% 的关税来回应最高法院的挫败，引发了新的法律挑战。

contentParagraphs.en: The new set of tariffs are intended to be more legally durable. Nonetheless more court fights could still be coming, meaning the question of whether tariffs will ultimately remain could continue to cast a shadow on businesses, warns Prasad.
contentParagraphs.zh: 新的关税政策旨在在法律上更加持久。尽管如此，普拉萨德警告说，更多的法庭斗争可能仍会到来，这意味着关税最终是否会继续存在的问题可能会继续给企业蒙上阴影。

contentParagraphs.en: "It is going to have a dampening effect on business investment," says Prasad. "Businesses crave certainty and this is going to introduce a whole lot of uncertainty which could potentially lead them to holding back from investment, which will [then] have some implications [on hiring]," he says.
contentParagraphs.zh: “这将对商业投资产生抑制作用，”普拉萨德说。 “企业渴望确定性，这将带来大量的不确定性，这可能会导致他们推迟投资，这将对[招聘]产生一些影响，”他说。

contentParagraphs.en: In addition, the administration is threatening additional tariffs, including one on pharmaceuticals and import duties on additional countries.
contentParagraphs.zh: 此外，政府还威胁征收额外关税，包括对药品征收关税和对其他国家征收进口关税。

contentParagraphs.en: 4. The administration argues there will be benefits — but at what cost?
contentParagraphs.zh: 4. 政府认为这会带来好处——但代价是什么？

contentParagraphs.en: Despite the warnings from economists and policy experts, the Trump administration has argued tariffs are vital as leverage to obtain key concessions from other countries on trade agreements.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管经济学家和政策专家发出警告，特朗普政府仍辩称，关税对于获得其他国家在贸易协定上的关键让步至关重要。

contentParagraphs.en: Trump has also argued tariffs will put pressure on American manufacturers to stop importing goods from other countries and instead start creating jobs in the U.S. However, despite tariffs that were imposed during his first term and since the beginning of his second, none of that has yet materialized.
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普还认为，关税将给美国制造商带来压力，迫使其停止从其他国家进口商品，转而开始在美国创造就业机会。然而，尽管在他的第一个任期内和第二个任期开始时征收了关税，但这些都还没有实现。

contentParagraphs.en: Tariffs, though, have brought more revenue from the government. The Budget Lab projects that tariffs will raise $1.9 trillion in revenue for the U.S.
contentParagraphs.zh: 不过，关税为政府带来了更多收入。预算实验室预计关税将为美国增加 1.9 万亿美元的收入

contentParagraphs.en: But Natasha Sarin, president of the Budget Lab argues, that revenue gains need to be weighed against the projected economic costs, including the uptick in inflation and a decline in economic growth.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但预算实验室主席娜塔莎·萨林认为，收入增长需要与预计的经济成本（包括通胀上升和经济增长下降）进行权衡。

contentParagraphs.en: "The way that [tariffs] are bringing in that revenue isn't incredibly efficient," she says. "The fact that the economy isn't growing as fast as it would be in a counterfactual world without tariffs levied at these levels, you never make up that. It's sort of a permanent decline in the economic strength as a result of this type of policy."
contentParagraphs.zh: “（关税）带来收入的方式效率并不高，”她说。 “事实是，经济增长速度不如不征收关税的反事实世界，这是无法弥补的。这种政策导致经济实力永久性下降。”

contentParagraphs.zh: 2026 年 1 月 13 日，特朗普参观了福特汽车公司位于密歇根州迪尔伯恩的红河综合体。

contentParagraphs.en: 5. The global economy could continue to bear the tariff fallout
contentParagraphs.zh: 5. 全球经济可能继续承受关税影响

contentParagraphs.en: Countries around the world face the prospect of continued pressure from the Trump administration.
contentParagraphs.zh: 世界各国都面临着特朗普政府持续施压的前景。

articles.title: Warning shot or publicity stunt - how worried should we be about the OpenAI hack?
articles.summary: Hugging Face said the hack was done at superhuman speed by an AI with little or no human guidance.
articles.titleZh: 警告镜头或宣传噱头——我们应该对 OpenAI 黑客攻击有多担心？
articles.summaryZh: Hugging Face 表示，这次黑客攻击是由人工智能以超人的速度完成的，几乎没有或根本没有人类指导。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, Getty ImagesByJoe TidyCyber correspondent, BBC World ServiceThis week the tech world was gripped by a story that has it all - and which started like a sci-fi thriller.Hugging Face - a kind of app store for artificial intelligence tools - announced on 16 July it had been hacked by a cyber criminal wielding enormously powerful AI.The bombshell announcement was full of scary, highly technical terms: "a swarm of sandboxes", "agentic attacker", and "self-migrating command and control".Hugging Face said the hack was different from anything it had handled before because it was done at superhuman speed by an AI with little or no human guidance.The AI performed 17,000 actions in less than two days, successfully breaching the large wealthy tech company to steal secrets.It left the tech world in shock. But who was responsible for this attack?Hugging Face researchers guessed the mysterious attackers had used one of the big AI models but they had no idea who or where the criminals were.The perplexed company contacted the police and investigations commenced.Who did it?Commentators and analysts took to their podcasts and social media accounts to guess which cyber crime group or nation state hacker might be behind it.Then on Wednesday, nearly a week after Hugging Face raised the alarm, the true culprit was unmasked.It was ChatGPT.The Scooby-Doo-style reveal was made even more bizarre - and worrying - because OpenAI said its bot did the whole thing on its own, without permission.The firm said it all went down during a test of its tech's hacking skills. Two new versions of ChatGPT, designed to be master hackers, broke out of a supposedly secure test environment and gained access to the internet.They then attacked Hugging Face to get access to the information to help them ace their exam.OpenAI issued a press release explaining what had happened and said it was "partnering with Hugging Face" to address the security incident and share lessons learned.Conspiracy dramaSince then, there has been fierce debate about the incident.Was it truly a stark warning about the future of AI? Or was it a publicity stunt by OpenAI to show off how powerful their models are?It's the kind of scare marketing AI companies have been accused of for years and, since the much discussed launch of Anthropic's Mythos model, cyber-security prowess has been a focal point.One of the top comments on OpenAI boss Sam Altman's X post about the incident summarises this scepticism: "If y'all can't understand that this was written to purely brag about the model then I don't know what to tell you."Figure caption, Watch: Why is the OpenAI cyber-attack so alarming?Cyber-security consultant Daniel Card said sarcastically on LinkedIn: "Isn't it lucky [that] out of the millions of sites that got pwn3d [hacked], OpenAI managed to pwn someone who also could benefit from the marketing exposure…"For some, the story is more conspiracy drama than sci-fi thriller. The message is: "Aren't my AI tools really powerful? Buy them so you can protect yourself from other people's AI attacks."We can't know the truth, but the opposing point of view posed by other commentators is just as dramatic. Is this a sign that OpenAI made a potentially dangerous error in judgement and planning?Comedy of errorsI've covered lots of AI stories, including the fears around Anthropic's Mythos model.My inbox is now chock full of cyber-security companies and experts criticising OpenAI for not building a stronger container to test its AI, known as a sandbox.After all, these AI agents had been trained specifically to hack into and out of places with no restrictions at all."The OpenAI and Hugging Face incident is a real-world example of a broader issue we've been highlighting for months," said Dor Sarig from Pillar Security. "Sandboxes alone are not a sufficient security boundary for agentic AI."Cyber security Professor Alan Woodward from Surrey University told reporters OpenAI had "egg on it's face", and Katie Moussouris from Luta Security went further, suggesting the AI industry is failing to control its dangerous inventions."We are working on cutting edge technology without the knowledge to contain it," she said. "Just because we have the smartest people developing AI does not mean we have the ability to do so safely."According to these views, if the hacking incident was a publicity stunt then it appears as though it backfired.Whatever led to the hack, it's clear this is a major moment for the AI industry and the cyber security world, which collided this year in ways people had been fearing for a long time.Addressing this fierce debate, AI and cyber security advisor Francesca Bosco said: "Two simplistic narratives are equally unhelpful: that this was a Hollywood-style escape, or that it was merely a publicity exercise. 日宣布，它已被一名拥有强大人工智能的网络犯罪分子入侵。这一爆炸性的公告充满了可怕的、高科技术语：“一群沙箱”、“代理攻击者”、 Hugging Face 表示，这次黑客攻击与之前处理过的任何事情都不同，因为它是由人工智能以超人的速度完成的，几乎没有或没有人类指导。人工智能在不到两天的时间内执行了 17,000 个操作，成功入侵了大型富裕科技公司并窃取了机密。这让科技界震惊了。但谁应对这次袭击负责？Hugging Face 研究人员猜测神秘攻击者使用了其中一个大型 AI 模型，但他们不知道罪犯是谁或在哪里。困惑的公司联系了警方并开始调查。是谁干的？评论员和分析师通过他们的播客和社交媒体帐户猜测背后可能是哪个网络犯罪组织或民族国家黑客。然后在周三，即 Hugging Face 发出警报近一周后，真正的罪魁祸首是这是 ChatGPT。史酷比式的揭露变得更加离奇和令人担忧，因为 OpenAI 表示其机器人在未经许可的情况下自行完成了整个事情。该公司表示，在测试其技术的黑客技能时，这一切都失败了。两个新版本的 ChatGPT 被设计成黑客高手，突破了所谓的安全测试环境并获得了互联网访问权限。他们随后攻击 Hugging Face，以获取信息以帮助他们在考试中取得好成绩。OpenAI 发布新闻稿解释了发生的事情，并表示正在“与 Hugging Face 合作”解决安全事件并分享经验教训。阴谋剧此后，有关该事件的激烈争论。这真的是对 AI 未来的严厉警告吗？或者这是 OpenAI 的一个宣传噱头，旨在炫耀他们的模型有多强大？多年来，人工智能公司一直被指控进行这种恐吓营销，自从 Anthropic 的 Mythos 模型推出以来，网络安全能力一直是人们关注的焦点。OpenAI 老板 Sam Altman 关于该事件的 X 帖子的热门评论之一总结了这种怀疑：“如果你们都不能理解这是纯粹为了吹嘘该模型而写的，那么我不知道该告诉你什么。”图标题，观看：为什么 OpenAI 网络攻击如此令人震惊？网络安全顾问 Daniel Card 在 LinkedIn 上讽刺地说：“在数百万个被 pwn3d [黑客攻击] 的网站中，OpenAI 成功地攻击了一个也可以从营销曝光中受益的人，这难道不是很幸运吗……”对某些人来说，这个故事更像是阴谋剧，而不是科幻惊悚片。传达的信息是：“我的人工智能工具不是真的很强大吗？购买它们，这样你就可以保护自己免受其他人的人工智能攻击。”我们无法知道真相，但其他评论员提出的反对观点同样引人注目。这是 OpenAI 在判断和规划方面犯下潜在危险错误的迹象吗？错误喜剧我已经报道了很多人工智能故事，包括对 Anthropic 神话模型的恐惧。我的收件箱现在塞满了网络安全公司和专家，批评 OpenAI 没有构建一个更强大的容器来测试其人工智能，即沙箱。毕竟，这些人工智能代理经过专门训练，可以毫无限制地进出任何地方。这是我们几个月来一直强调的更广泛问题的现实例子。”Pillar Security 的 Dor Sarig 说道。萨里大学的网络安全教授艾伦·伍德沃德（Alan Woodward）告诉记者，OpenAI“脸上有鸡蛋”，而来自 Luta Security 的凯蒂·穆苏里斯（Katie Moussouris）更进一步，表明人工智能行业未能控制其危险的发明。“我们正在研究尖端技术，但不具备遏制它的知识，”她说。 “仅仅因为我们有最聪明的人开发人工智能，并不意味着我们有能力安全地这样做。”根据这些观点，如果黑客事件是一种宣传噱头，那么它似乎会适得其反。无论导致黑客攻击的原因是什么，很明显，这对人工智能行业和网络安全世界来说都是一个重要时刻，今年它们以人们长期以来担心的方式发生了冲突。在谈到这场激烈的辩论时，人工智能和网络安全顾问弗朗西斯卡博斯科说：“两个简单化的叙述同样无济于事：这是一次好莱坞式的逃亡，或者只是一场宣传活动。“更严肃的解释是，压力测试暴露了遏制和评估架构中的弱点。”灾难电影这一事件是人工智能代理失控的一系列令人担忧和奇怪的例子中的最新一个。在最近的研究中，英国人工智能安全研究所 articles.title: ADHD has rewired the workplace. This is what it means for bosses and workers
articles.summary: As ADHD diagnoses have risen, have workplaces caught up with the needs of the workforce?
articles.titleZh: ADHD 改变了工作场所。这对老板和工人来说意味着什么
articles.summaryZh: 随着多动症诊断的增加，工作场所是否满足了劳动力的需求？

contentParagraphs.en: Taking one of the UK's biggest grocery chains to an employment tribunal was something that Ryan Toghill says almost took over his life."It was all I could think about for 18 months and more," he says.The deputy store manager at Lidl, who'd told his bosses he'd been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), was called to a disciplinary meeting after breaking company rules by using equipment he hadn't been trained to use. After that meeting, Ryan was dismissed for gross misconduct.He successfully appealed the decision and was offered a lower-paid role. He rejected it and took his case to a tribunal. Eventually, he was awarded more than £45,000 when the judge found his former employer hadn't fully taken his ADHD diagnosis into account during the disciplinary process.The judgement found reasonable adjustments during the process hadn't been offered to him, such as additional breaks.He'd been described by a manager as showing "a lack of remorse," something the tribunal found was clearly linked with his communication differences associated with having ADHD."I don't show a lot of emotions," Ryan explains. "I could be incredibly happy, angry, upset, or remorseful, and my facial expressions and tone of voice would essentially remain the same."The tribunal upheld part of his claims for unfair dismissal, wrongful dismissal and a failure to make reasonable adjustments. Lidl says it's "committed to ensuring that everyone receives the reasonable adjustments, clear communication and support they need to thrive."Campaigners, lawyers and HR teams say cases like this highlight a shift that businesses should be paying attention to.Thousands of people have been diagnosed as neurodivergent in the last few years, an umbrella term that covers autism, ADHD and other conditions such as dyslexia and Tourette's syndrome.Since the pandemic in particular, diagnosis rates for ADHD and autism have been rising, and they're featuring more regularly in disputes in employment tribunals.Similarly, research by King's College London last year suggested that around 90% of autistic people over 40 remain undiagnosed.Diagnosis levels aside, there has been a huge increase in awareness of the challenges neurodivergent people can face - whether it's in communication preferences, personal organisation, or sensory needs. In workplaces, many describe "masking," a term which means trying to hide their traits in order to fit in - something which can put a huge strain on the person's wellbeing."Society is playing catch-up," says Ben Branson, an entrepreneur who runs a charity called The Hidden 20%, which campaigns for better understanding of neurodivergence. He was diagnosed with autism in 2022."The recognition of adult neurodivergence has exploded," he says. "But we have always been here, we are just not hiding anymore, and there are millions of people finally understanding why they kept moving jobs, why they didn't fit, why they kept burning out and why they felt so exhausted, who are no longer willing to struggle in silence."This year's City and Guilds Foundation's Neurodiversity Index found that while employers think they're "doing better" when it comes to inclusion, neurodivergent employees say they are seeing only small improvements.This disconnect between managers and staff is something employment lawyer Jodie Hill is familiar with. Her firm, Thrive Law, specialises in workplace wellbeing and works with both employees and businesses. She set it up in 2018 after getting her own ADHD diagnosis at the age of 35."In the last three months, I've seen more than I've ever seen before in terms of enquiries," she says.So, what are some employers doing that leads to successful action being taken against them? Hill says one thing that comes up a lot is bosses asking for proof of a formal diagnosis, when this isn't the legal test. Another issue can be an employer looking to dismiss someone over performance before considering a possible disability. Both of which could leave them exposed to claims of discrimination.In the training sessions she carries out for businesses, she says she hears from the employer's perspective that it can feel like "every other conversation is about people wanting support".Fears over cost, and concern that doing something for one member of staff means they have to do it for all of them, can lead to what Hill describes as an "initial dismissiveness" from some employers. But that, she says, comes from a lack of understanding over what can be an "internal and invisible" struggle."There's a mindset from employers that it's very linear… and that all the symptoms are the same every day," she says.Another challenge can be determining what constitutes a "reasonable adjustment," a sticking point which can be what ends up being decided in a tribunal.Hill says some employers "don't know where to start" and wrongly assume that making reasonable adjustments means doing whatever the employee asks.Some tribunals have shown the limits of what's "reasonable." In one case, an autistic claimant had requested extensive changes to the recruitment process at the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC), including simplified questions and advance access to test questions. The JAC had already offered extra time and assistance from a friend and denied the extra requests. When it went to tribunal, the judge found the adjustments the person had asked for were "clearly going beyond what was necessary or reasonable".While there isn't a check list for employers, lawyers stress that they have to be able to justify why they're saying no to something, and show they've looked at alternative options.Jo Moseley from law firm Irwin Mitchell explains that when it comes to judging what is "reasonable", a tribunal would take into account factors like the person's role, and the size of the business."Big employers will certainly be expected to do more than small employers," she says, stressing that many adjustments can cost nothing or very

articles.summaryZh: 这次中断影响了玩家在 PlayStation 上启动游戏、应用程序或网络功能的能力。

contentParagraphs.en: A PlayStation Network outage which left some gamers unable to play digital games for hours has been resolved. According to Down Detector, which tracks outages, tens of thousands of people reported problems globally, external with the service on Friday.The outage, which affected gamers' ability to launch games, apps or network features on their PlayStation, prompted some to highlight their concerns around Sony's plans to no longer release new PlayStation games on discs from January 2028.By Friday evening, all affected services were up and running, according to Sony's status page, external. The BBC has approached PlayStation for comment."Can't play digital games till you fix it. Yet I can put my disc in and play. The all digital future looks great," read one comment on X, external earlier on Friday.Sony said in a blog post earlier this month, external that new games would still be able to be bought in shops, but they would come with a digital code.The problems began to appear around the same time as an alert from Amazon Web Services that some servers were facing issues, which was earlier resolved., external
contentParagraphs.zh: 导致一些玩家数小时无法玩数字游戏的 PlayStation 网络中断问题已得到解决。据跟踪中断情况的 Down Detector 称，周五全球有数万人报告了该服务的问题。这次中断影响了游戏玩家在 PlayStation 上启动游戏、应用程序或网络功能的能力，促使一些人强调了他们对索尼计划从 2028 年 1 月起不再发布新的 PlayStation 光盘游戏的担忧。根据索尼的外部状态页面，到周五晚上，所有受影响的服务都已启动并运行。 BBC 已联系 PlayStation 征求意见。周五早些时候，X 上的一条评论写道：“在你修复它之前，我不能玩数字游戏。但我可以把光盘放进去玩。全数字化的未来看起来很棒。”索尼在本月早些时候的一篇博客文章中表示，新游戏仍然可以在商店购买，但它们会附带数字代码。这些问题开始出现的时间与亚马逊网络服务发出的警报差不多是一样的，即一些服务器面临问题，该问题已于早些时候得到解决。

articles.title: Faisal Islam: The UK's Trump trade deal no longer looks world-beating
articles.summary: While the US tariffs imposed on the UK are effectively unchanged, other countries now have a better deal.
articles.titleZh: 费萨尔·伊斯兰：英国的特朗普贸易协议看起来不再是世界一流的
articles.summaryZh: 尽管美国对英国征收的关税实际上没有变化，但其他国家现在有了更好的协议。

contentParagraphs.en: It has been a long road for President Donald Trump as he looks for a justification to erect a tariff wall around the US, including against key allies.From the opioid crisis to illegal migration, then the need to bring manufacturing back to America's shores, the list goes on.Through Trump's second term, there has been a new justification almost every month for the trade levies he is seeking to place on allies.Some have been overturned by the courts, others by economics and some even by their own logic. And so, Trump has now turned to effectively accusing dozens of trade partners of trading in goods that have been produced using forced labour.These are "tariffs in search of an authority", as one industry figure put it. The forced labour line shores up President Trump's tariffs against a challenge from Congress or the courts.In practice, the levies are curiously similar by country to a previous round of tariffs imposed supposedly for completely different reasons.The good news for the UK is that the regime effectively remains the same as before.What has changed is that our nearest neighbours in the European Union now have a much better deal than before, and in turn are in a better situation than the UK.While the UK and the EU each appear to have a 10% rate, the EU's is a flat rate, while the UK's will apply alongside other tariffs, in a range of goods including footwear and textiles.The government has struck effective side deals on medicines, steel, aluminium, cars and, with the help of King Charles, whisky.At the end of this process however the overall trade-weighted effective tariff rate for the EU (8.5%) could end up a bit lower than the UK's (6.8%).It should not matter that much, but the help given by doing the first deal, and by post-Brexit trade freedoms, looks to have been short-lived.The British Chambers of Commerce trade expert William Bain points to the competitive advantage for EU exporters into the US in some sectors.The EU has secured better treatment because it has passed a ban on forced labour goods, which the UK has not.This is not an accusation on the use of forced labour in supply chains. It is about the passing of specific legislation, mirroring the US ban on products that have used forced labour in supply chains.There should be scope for a better deal for the UK, but it raises an interesting question about whether the government will pursue an EU-style ban. This is widely seen as a backdoor way to target China, in particular for conditions in its Xinjiang province.Last October, external the government said it "remained firmly opposed to the use of state-imposed forced labour", but that it was "considering how best to reflect this position," citing "operational and legal complexities".Since then, the UK has welcomed imports of Chinese cars, and is exploring a services trade deal with the country. The relationship with China has been a balancing act for the government.This is also one of the global stories of the tariff wars. As the US repeatedly changes its rationale for tariffs, the rest of the world is focused on trading with each other. For example, Canada increased its trade with the rest of the world by more than it lost from the US.China's total dollar trade with the US is flat in the first half of this year versus last year. Across the world it is up 21%, including 14% with the EU, 11% with the UK, and 24% with Africa.There could be pressure now to legislate for a formal ban on forced labour products. Successive governments have opted for a lighter voluntary due diligence regime.Will the US force a change in the UK and elsewhere, and what might it offer in return?Or the UK may opt to keep its precarious geopolitical position by sticking to its existing deals in medicines, metals and cars.

articles.title: Dodging snipers, housing crisis forces Yemenis to live on front line
articles.summary: Living near Taiz's front line forces families to make difficult choices amid sniper threats and economic hardships.
articles.titleZh: 躲避狙击手、住房危机迫使也门人生活在前线
articles.summaryZh: 生活在塔伊兹前线附近的家庭被迫在狙击手威胁和经济困难的情况下做出艰难的选择。

contentParagraphs.en: Taiz, Yemen – Um Yousef knew that living on the front line in Taiz was dangerous. The area had been quieter for the past few years thanks to a general de-escalation of the war in Yemen, but it still lay between territory controlled by Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels.Destroyed buildings mark the city’s front line areas, evidence of the brutal fighting that has lasted for more than a decade.Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Oman talking with Tehran on Hormuz as US and Iran continue strikeslist 2 of 3Yemen’s valleys and farms are full of dangerous plastic wastelist 3 of 3US attacks Iran as Houthis allow Chinese ships to pass: What’s the latest?end of listBut Um Yousef felt that she didn’t have a choice. A single mother of four children in her 40s, she couldn’t afford the typical market rate of about $130 for a three-bedroom house in the central Yemeni city. Her husband died years ago while working abroad, so she was the sole breadwinner for the family in a country where poverty has increased sharply since the war began more than a decade ago.“There is a huge demand for houses, and all my efforts failed while I was living in a single room with my children,” recalled Um Yousef, who asked to use a pseudonym for security reasons. “It was very difficult to stay in that one room.”After eight months of moving from one area to another, and even searching on the outskirts of Taiz, she ultimately decided that her only option was a home near the front line. Yes, it was dangerous, but with little money coming in, the home she found for about $13 a month couldn’t be ignored.In January 2025, the family made the move. Two months later, her 11-year-old son came into the house from playing outside with blood pouring out of his mouth – he’d been shot.Sniper danger“I couldn’t understand what happened – I didn’t hear any gunfire,” Um Yousef said.She still doesn’t know the exact cause of the shooting, but many of the casualties near Yemen’s front lines are the result of sniper fire.Taiz is particularly dangerous in this regard. The front line going through the city is one of the few in the country in an urban area. The city’s geography, hilly and with a mountain overlooking it, offers numerous vantage points for snipers.A United Nations monitoring project found that 66 percent of all civilian casualties from sniper shootings in Yemen last year were in Taiz. Of the 21 cases recorded, nine were children.Thankfully, Um Yousef’s son’s injuries were not as serious as first feared. After being immediately taken to hospital, he received medical treatment and was discharged the next day.The incident woke Um Yousef up to the reality of where she had brought her children to. But she still can’t afford to move. Instead, she has had no choice but to stay and learn ways to reduce the risk.“Residents here take precautions I wasn’t aware of, like turning off lights at night in rooms visible from a distance, and keeping children from playing in open areas,” she explained. “They have to play behind the houses instead. I’m aware of these things now and follow them to keep my children safe.”Even in the safe parts of Taiz, damaged homes remain, with the pace of reconstruction in the Yemeni city slow [Al Jazeera]Damaged homesTaiz governorate is the most populous in Yemen, with a population of almost 4.5 million and more than 400,000 internally displaced people, according to Khalid Alwan, director of the local statistics office.“More than 10,000 houses were completely or partially damaged by the conflict in Taiz, and there are many more we couldn’t reach to count,” Alwan told Al Jazeera. “Reconstruction is expensive, and most residents cannot afford to repair their homes even if they are in safe areas. This further worsens the housing crisis in the city.”He noted that while some humanitarian organisations have repaired partially damaged homes in safe areas, these efforts are a drop in the ocean compared with the sheer number of affected properties.The Nahda Makers Organisation (NMO) is one such group rehabilitating homes in several Yemeni governorates. To date, NMO has repaired 2,389 houses in Taiz, Lahj, Hodeidah, Aden and Abyan governorates – the vast majority of them in Taiz.While this initiative has helped some families return to safe areas, the overall need remains overwhelming, with an estimated 4.8 million displaced people across the country still unable to return.One of the partially damaged houses in Taiz rehabilitated with support from UNHCR and the Nahda Makers Organisation [Courtesy: Nahda Makers Organisation]HousesittingMohammed Saeed has been living in the al-Thawrah neighbourhood of Taiz near the front line since 2023. He believes the war has taken a heavy toll on society, with soaring rents being one of its worst consequences.“I’m not happy living here as we frequently hear the sounds of gunfire at night. Even if we aren’t targeted, just hearing it is enough to terrify us,” the 53-year-old told Al Jazeera. “In the beginning, my children couldn’t sleep when they heard the shooting, but now they’ve adapted. Adapted to what? Adapted to living in a dangerous area.”Mohammed, who is unemployed and cannot afford rent, lives in a house for free in exchange for guarding it. Because the neighbourhood is near the front lines, many residents here do not pay rent.“Nowadays it is calm, but if there is any escalation, we will be trapped in the crossfire,” Mohammed said. “I hope I can find a job that enables me to rent a house in a safe place and leave this one.”Khalid Abdulhadi, 46, is one of the people who could afford to leave. He was born in the al-Kamb neighbourhood of Taiz city and owns a house there. However, he fled during the heavy fighting in 2018 and has not returned, as the proximity to the front line makes it far too unsafe.“It is not the right decision to return and live in a dangerous area,” he told Al Jazeera. “Even though I am paying rent while owning my own home, going back could cost me my l

“住在那个房间里非常困难。”经过八个月的从一个地区搬到另一个地区，甚至在塔伊兹郊区寻找，她最终决定她唯一的选择是在前线附近的一所房子。是的，这很危险，但由于收入很少，她每月花费约 13 美元找到的房子也不容忽视。 2025 年 1 月，一家人搬了家。两个月后，她11岁的儿子在外面玩耍回到家中，嘴里流着血——他被枪杀了。 狙击手危险 “我不明白发生了什么——我没有听到任何枪声，”乌姆·优素福说。她仍然不知道枪击事件的具体原因，但也门前线附近的许多伤亡都是狙击手开火造成的。塔伊兹在这方面尤其危险。前线穿过城市，是全国为数不多的市区之一。这座城市的地形地势崎岖，山峦叠翠，为狙击手提供了众多有利位置。联合国监测项目发现，去年也门狙击手枪击事件造成的平民伤亡中，66% 发生在塔伊兹。在记录的 21 例病例中，有 9 例是儿童。值得庆幸的是，Um Yousef 儿子的伤势并不像最初担心的那么严重。乌姆·尤瑟夫立即被送往医院接受治疗，并于第二天出院。这一事件让乌姆·优素福醒悟到她带孩子去了哪里的现实。但她还是搬不起。相反，她别无选择，只能留下来学习降低风险的方法。“这里的居民采取了我没有意识到的预防措施，比如晚上关掉远处可见房间的灯，并阻止孩子在空旷的地方玩耍，”她解释道。 “他们必须在房子后面玩耍。我现在意识到了这些事情，并跟随他们以确保我的孩子们的安全。”即使在塔伊兹的安全地区，受损的房屋仍然存在，也门城市的重建速度缓慢 [半岛电视台]受损的房屋塔伊兹省是也门人口最多的省，有近 450 万人口和超过 40 万国内流离失所者，当地统计局局长哈立德·阿尔万表示阿尔万告诉半岛电视台：“塔伊兹的冲突导致一万多所房屋完全或部分受损，还有更多的房屋我们无法统计。” articles.title: Trump vows to investigate EU over fining of US tech companies
articles.summary: The US president says fines against Google, as well as Apple, Meta and Amazon, should be "entirely reversed."
articles.titleZh: 特朗普发誓要调查欧盟对美国科技公司的罚款
articles.summaryZh: 美国总统表示，针对谷歌、苹果、Meta 和亚马逊的罚款应该“完全撤销”。

contentParagraphs.en: Donald Trump says the US will launch an investigation into the European Union and threatened a fresh tariff over fines handed to some of the biggest American tech companies. It comes days after the European Commission fined Google €890m ($1bn) for operating in a way that squeezed out competitors to its services.In a post to Truth Social, which Trump owns, the US president said the EU would pay a "very big price" over how it had treated Google, along with other major US tech companies Apple, Meta, and Amazon, which have also been investigated."The United States of America is not a "PIGGYBANK" for Europe, nor will we allow it to be!" he wrote.Trump said any fines should be "entirely reversed" and that he was initiating a trade investigation of the EU while considering "a substantial TARIFF".He added that the US would "immediately initiate a 301 investigation" over European regulators' alleged practice of "robbing American companies and, in turn, the American taxpayer". Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, external gives The Office of the United States Trade Representative the power to react and investigate trade practices believed to be unfair. The second Trump Administration has launched several such investigations, external since last year.The tariff threat comes just one day after Trump announced new tariffs on 60 trading partners, including the EU, UK and China, of between 10% and 12.5%. Trump also last month threatened a 100% import tariff on any European country that introduces a digital services tax on American technology giants, despite many such nations already doing so, external for years.Major tech companies, including Google, Meta, Apple, and Amazon, have donated millions of dollars to funds behind Trump's campaign and presidency. José Castañeda, a spokesman for Google, told the BBC the company had "worked hard to comply" with Europe's Digital Markets Act but had "expressed our concerns about the impact of recent EC decisions"."We appreciate the engagement by the administration and US government," Castañeda added.In addition to the recent fine against Google, Trump claimed in his post that Apple had received EU fines of $15bn, Meta fines of $3bn, and Amazon fines of $2.5bn. Representatives of Meta, Apple and Amazon, as well as the European Commission, have been contacted for comment.It was not clear where the figures cited by Trump come from. Shortly before Trump was elected president in 2024, he said Tim Cook, Apple's chief executive, had called him directly to complain about fines the company had received from European regulators.The call came not long after Apple lost a long-running dispute over unpaid taxes.Meta, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has been fined several times by EU regulators, including for violations of user privacy and competition laws, external. It is also facing new fines over purportedly "addictive" features of its apps. Meta last year said the EU was "attempting to handicap successful American businesses".Amazon, however, appears to have been investigated at times by the European Commission, but avoided major fines. The company in 2022 reached an agreement with regulators to change some of its practices in Europe. A separate regulatory body in Luxembourg did impose on Amazon a fine of more than $800mn for violations of General Data Protection Regulation rules, but that was overturned last year, external.
contentParagraphs.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国将对欧盟展开调查，并威胁对美国一些最大科技公司的罚款征收新关税。几天前，欧盟委员会因谷歌以排挤竞争对手的方式运营而对其服务进行了8.9亿欧元（10亿美元）的罚款。在特朗普拥有的Truth Social上发表的一篇文章中，美国总统表示，欧盟将为其对待谷歌以及其他美国主要科技公司苹果、Meta和亚马逊的方式付出“非常大的代价”，这些公司也受到了调查。“美利坚合众国不是欧洲的‘存钱罐’，我们也不会允许这样的事情发生！”他写道。特朗普表示，任何罚款都应该“完全撤销”，他正在对欧盟发起贸易调查，同时考虑“大幅关税”。他补充说，美国将“立即启动301调查”，指控欧洲监管机构“抢劫美国公司，进而掠夺美国纳税人”的做法。 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条“外部”赋予美国贸易代表办公室做出反应和调查被认为不公平的贸易行为的权力。自去年以来，特朗普第二届政府已启动多项此类外部调查。就在特朗普宣布对包括欧盟、英国和中国在内的 60 个贸易伙伴征收 10% 至 12.5% 的新关税一天后，就发出了关税威胁。特朗普上个月还威胁要对任何对美国科技巨头征收数字服务税的欧洲国家征收100%的进口关税，尽管许多这样的国家多年来已经这样做了。包括谷歌、Meta、苹果和亚马逊在内的主要科技公司已向特朗普的竞选和总统任期捐赠了数百万美元。谷歌发言人何塞·卡斯塔涅达 (José Castañeda) 告诉 BBC，该公司“努力遵守”欧洲数字市场法案，但“表达了我们对欧盟委员会最近决定的影响的担忧”。卡斯塔涅达补充道，“我们感谢政府和美国政府的参与。”除了最近对谷歌的罚款外，特朗普还在帖子中声称，苹果已收到欧盟 150 亿美元的罚款、Meta 30 亿美元的罚款和亚马逊 30 亿美元的罚款。 25亿美元。已联系 Meta、苹果和亚马逊以及欧盟委员会的代表征求意见。目前尚不清楚特朗普引用的数据来自哪里。特朗普在 2024 年当选总统前不久，他表示，苹果首席执行官蒂姆·库克曾直接打电话给他，抱怨该公司收到欧洲监管机构的罚款。这一电话是在苹果因未缴税款的长期纠纷败诉后不久发出的。拥有 Facebook、Instagram 和 WhatsApp 的 Meta 已多次被欧盟监管机构罚款，包括违反用户隐私和竞争法等外部行为。它还因其应用程序据称“令人上瘾”的功能而面临新的罚款。 Meta去年表示，欧盟“试图阻碍成功的美国企业”。然而，亚马逊似乎曾多次受到欧盟委员会的调查，但避免了重大罚款。该公司于 2022 年与监管机构达成协议，改变其在欧洲的一些做法。卢森堡的一个独立监管机构确实因亚马逊违反《通用数据保护条例》规则而对亚马逊处以超过 8 亿美元的罚款，但去年这一处罚被外部推翻。

articles.title: U.S. allies hit with new tariffs object to Trump's forced labor allegations
articles.summary: Australia and the European Union were among U.S. trade partners who criticized the tariffs.
articles.titleZh: 受到新关税打击的美国盟友反对特朗普的强迫劳动指控
articles.summaryZh: 澳大利亚和欧盟等美国贸易伙伴对关税提出了批评。

contentParagraphs.en: President Trump speaks during an event to announce new tariffs in the Rose Garden at the White House on April 2, 2025.
contentParagraphs.zh: 2025年4月2日，特朗普总统在白宫玫瑰园宣布新关税的活动中发表讲话。

contentParagraphs.en: Many of America's key allies on Friday criticized the U.S. administration's new tariffs against them, after President Trump renewed the tax on imports from more than 60 countries just as the previous tariffs expired.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国的许多主要盟友周五批评了美国政府对他们征收的新关税，此前特朗普总统在之前的关税到期后重新对来自60多个国家的进口产品征税。

contentParagraphs.en: The U.S. Supreme Court had ruled earlier this year that many of the tariffs imposed under emergency powers were unconstitutional.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国最高法院今年早些时候裁定，根据紧急权力征收的许多关税都是违宪的。

contentParagraphs.en: The president cited lax enforcement of a ban on the use of forced labor to produce goods as his reason for renewing the tariffs, an allegation Australia and the European Union vehemently rejected.
contentParagraphs.zh: 总统将使用强迫劳动生产商品的禁令执行不力作为他延长关税的理由，澳大利亚和欧盟强烈反对。

contentParagraphs.en: Those targeted with the latest penalties face between 10% and 12.5% on many of their exports to the U.S., although various countries have trade deal exemptions for certain sectors.
contentParagraphs.zh: 那些受到最新处罚的国家对美国的许多出口面临10 ％至12.5 ％的罚款，尽管各国对某些行业有贸易协定豁免。

contentParagraphs.en: "Trading partners that have made commitments to adopt, and effectively enforce, forced labor import prohibitions will have a 10% tariff, and trading partners that have failed to adopt a forced labor import prohibition will have a 12.5% tariff rate," according to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国贸易代表办公室表示： “承诺采用并有效执行强迫劳动进口禁令的贸易伙伴将征收10%的关税，而未能采用强迫劳动进口禁令的贸易伙伴将征收12.5%的关税。”

contentParagraphs.en: Here are some reactions from around the world:
contentParagraphs.zh: 以下是来自世界各地的一些反应：

contentParagraphs.en: Australia and New Zealand
contentParagraphs.zh: 澳大利亚和新西兰

contentParagraphs.en: Australian Trade Minister Don Farrell said the 12.5% tariffs on his country's exports to the U.S. were "unjustified" and called it "an extremely disappointing decision."
contentParagraphs.zh: 澳大利亚贸易部长唐·法雷尔(Don Farrell)表示，澳大利亚对美国出口征收12.5%的关税是“不合理的” ，并称这是“一个非常令人失望的决定”。

contentParagraphs.en: "We believe we do take the issue of modern slavery seriously. We have some of the most progressive legislation anywhere in the world. We say that these tariffs are unjustified and we call on the United States government to reverse them," Farrell said to Sky News.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们相信我们确实认真对待现代奴隶制问题。我们有一些世界上最进步的立法。我们说这些关税是不合理的，我们呼吁美国政府撤销这些关税，”法雷尔对天空新闻说。

contentParagraphs.en: In New Zealand, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon called the tariffs "extremely disappointing."
contentParagraphs.zh: 在新西兰，总理克里斯托弗·卢克松（ Christopher Luxon ）称关税“非常令人失望”。

contentParagraphs.en: "The U.S. investigation did not provide meaningful evidence to support claims in relation to forced labour. Tariffs are not the way — they drive up costs and uncertainty for businesses," he said online.
contentParagraphs.zh: “美国的调查没有提供有意义的证据来支持与强迫劳动有关的主张。关税不是办法，它们推高了企业的成本和不确定性，”他在网上说。

contentParagraphs.en: European Union and the United Kingdom
contentParagraphs.zh: 欧盟和英国

contentParagraphs.en: The EU's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, also questioned Trump's rationale for the new tariffs.
contentParagraphs.zh: 欧盟外交政策负责人卡贾·卡拉斯（ Kaja Kallas ）也质疑特朗普征收新关税的理由。

contentParagraphs.en: "If you compare our labor laws to the ones of the United States, I mean, we have, people have paid vacations, we have very good conditions, labor conditions, for our employees, so it's not really grounded," she told Reuters.
contentParagraphs.zh: “如果你将我们的劳动法与美国的劳动法进行比较，我的意思是，我们有，人们有带薪假期，我们有非常好的条件，劳动条件，为我们的员工，所以它不是真正的接地，”她告诉路透社。

contentParagraphs.en: Shipping containers are seen ready for transport at the Guangzhou Port in the Nansha district in southern China's Guangdong province, April 17, 2025.
contentParagraphs.zh: 2025年4月17日，在中国南方广东省南沙区的广州港，集装箱已准备好运输。

contentParagraphs.en: The British government said Trump's latest 10% tariffs will amount to "no negative change" for British exports. Former Prime Minister Keir Starmer was able to strike a better U.S. trade deal than many other countries, with lower tariff rates. And King Charles III got the U.S. tariff on Scotch whisky reduced to zero when he visited the White House in April.
contentParagraphs.zh: 英国政府表示，特朗普最近的10 ％关税将对英国出口构成“没有负面变化”。前总理基尔·斯塔默（ Keir Starmer ）能够以较低的关税率达成比许多其他国家更好的美国贸易协议。国王查理三世在4月访问白宫时将美国对苏格兰威士忌的关税降至零。

contentParagraphs.en: But the British government said in a statement: "We take forced labour very seriously to ensure that in global supply chains U.K. businesses are not complicit."
contentParagraphs.zh: 但英国政府在一份声明中表示： “我们非常重视强迫劳动，以确保英国企业在全球供应链中不会成为同谋。”

contentParagraphs.en: The world's second-largest economy, China, was hit with 12.5% new tariffs and the Foreign Ministry condemned the move.
contentParagraphs.zh: 世界第二大经济体中国受到12.5%新关税的打击，外交部谴责此举。

contentParagraphs.en: "Tariff wars and trade wars do not serve any parties' interests," ministry spokesman Lin Jian told a regular press conference on Friday.
contentParagraphs.zh: “关税战和贸易战不符合任何一方的利益，”该部发言人林健周五在例行新闻发布会上说。

contentParagraphs.en: Japan will also see 12.5% tariffs on exports to the U.S. Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said his country had been reassured by the Trump administration that its goods would not be slapped with more tariffs.
contentParagraphs.zh: 日本还将对向美国出口商品征收12.5%的关税。日本内阁官房长官木原实表示，特朗普政府已经向日本保证，其商品不会被征收更多关税。

contentParagraphs.en: "It is regrettable that the measure imposes tariffs on the grounds of nonexistence of measures banning imports of goods made by forced labor, even though Japan's industry and trade are in line with international rules," he said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说： “令人遗憾的是，该措施以不存在禁止进口强迫劳动产品的措施为由征收关税，尽管日本的工业和贸易符合国际规则。”

contentParagraphs.en: Trump's latest tariffs stacked a 12.5% duty on many imports from Brazil — just days after putting 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods.
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普的最新关税对来自巴西的许多进口产品征收了12.5%的关税--就在对巴西商品征收25%关税的几天后。

contentParagraphs.en: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said in a statement that his government "rejects" the measure, saying the U.S. "manipulated" human rights issues to support a "protectionist trade policy." He said Brazil has ratified dozens more international labor treaties than the United States has.
contentParagraphs.zh: 巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦（ Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ）在一份声明中表示，巴西政府“拒绝”这项措施，称美国“操纵”人权问题以支持“保护主义贸易政策”。“他说，巴西批准的国际劳工条约比美国多了几十个。

contentParagraphs.en: Trump has often tussled with Brazil's left-wing government. But other South American countries with more pro-Trump presidents, including Chile, also got the higher 12.5% tariff.
contentParagraphs.zh: 特朗普经常与巴西左翼政府争执不休。但其他拥有更多亲特朗普总统的南美国家，包括智利，也获得了更高的12.5%的关税。

contentParagraphs.en: The U.S. slapped a 10% tariff on its top trading partner Mexico. But Mexican Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard said his country will see no change since there has already been a 10% tariff, and more than 80% of Mexico's exports to the U.S. enter duty free under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国对其最大贸易伙伴墨西哥征收10%的关税。但墨西哥经济部长马塞洛·埃布拉德（ Marcelo Ebrard ）表示，他的国家不会发生任何变化，因为已经征收了10 ％的关税，墨西哥对美国的出口中有80 ％以上根据美国-墨西哥-加拿大协议免税。

contentParagraphs.en: Lauren Frayer contributed to this story from London, Kristina Kukolja contributed from Melbourne, Australia, and Catherine Osborn contributed from Rio de Janeiro.
contentParagraphs.zh: Lauren Frayer来自伦敦， Kristina Kukolja来自澳大利亚墨尔本， Catherine Osborn来自里约热内卢。
