articles.title: Wildfires in Spain and France force evacuation of 200,000 people
articles.summary: France has appealed for international help, while Spain has declared a national emergency.
articles.titleZh: 西班牙和法国山火迫使20万人疏散
articles.summaryZh: 法国已呼吁国际社会提供帮助，而西班牙则宣布全国进入紧急状态。

contentParagraphs.en: France has appealed for international help, while Spain has declared a national emergency.Nearly 200,000 people have been forced from their homes and holiday resorts in the face of massive, uncontained wildfires in France and Spain.Spanish firefighters hoped to get control of wildfires raging near capital Madrid on Saturday, but an official warned that erratic winds threatened to fan the blazes further, as thick grey smoke filled the sky west of the city.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Spanish police accuse tractor driver of sparking wildfire as blazes spreadlist 2 of 4Wildfire survivors tell of narrow escape as Spain declares emergencylist 3 of 4Wildfires force evacuation of tens of thousands in France and Spainlist 4 of 4Thousands forced to evacuate as wildfires sweep across southern Franceend of listCarlos Novillo, the Madrid regional government’s emergency management chief, said the wildfire near the capital was “at its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain”.Two separate wildfires combined on Friday to become one huge blaze, which was close to merging with yet another in the neighbouring Castilla y Leon region.Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez was scheduled to attend an emergency planning meeting on Saturday morning in Cenicientos, a village at the heart of the fire zone, and speak to the media afterwards.In France, authorities on Saturday evacuated thousands of people ⁠from suburbs ⁠near Bordeaux as wildfires in areas around the city showed no ⁠signs of abating.Sophie Brocas, who heads the local administration of La Nouvelle-Aquitaine et ⁠de la Gironde, which covers the Bordeaux region, said the areas of Le Haillan, Eysines and Merignac were being cleared out.The Bordeaux region is famed for its vineyards and the ‌city is one of the main transport hubs for tourists visiting nearby holiday resorts on the Atlantic coast.Around 44,000 people fled the upmarket Cap Ferret peninsula south of Bordeaux, with the only road threatened by flames.Boats moved hundreds of people away from the fires, while others drove off the peninsula, known for its millionaire residences. More than 50 houses there have been destroyed.French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said more than 141,000 people had so far been evacuated from the Gironde and Landes regions.“The fires which ⁠are hitting our country have reached a level that has never been seen before,” Lecornu wrote on X ⁠on Saturday.The French army has also been drafted in ⁠to help, while Macron has asked the European Union for help.At least 141,000 people have been evacuated in southwestern France and 25,000 in the Madrid region, among them more than 1,200 elderly and disabled people, French and Spanish officials said.Some European regions have suffered at least two heatwaves since May. And drought blamed on human-fuelled climate change has heightened the threat from wildfires this year, the World Weather Attribution group said in a study published this week.
contentParagraphs.zh: 法国已呼吁国际社会提供帮助，而西班牙则宣布全国进入紧急状态。面对法国和西班牙爆发的大规模、无法控制的山火，近20万人被迫离开家园和度假胜地。周六，西班牙消防队员希望控制首都马德里附近肆虐的山火，但一名官员警告称，不稳定的风势可能会进一步煽动火势，城市西边的天空弥漫着浓浓的灰色烟雾。 推荐故事列表 4 itemslist 1 of 4西班牙警方指控拖拉机司机在大火蔓延时引发野火list 2 of 4野火幸存者讲述西班牙宣布进入紧急状态后侥幸逃脱list 4中的3野火迫使法国和西班牙数万人疏散list 4中的4数千人被迫撤离，因为野火席卷法国南部listend of 马德里地区政府应急管理负责人卡洛斯·诺维洛(Carlos Novillo)表示，首都附近的野火是“火势达到顶峰，目前超出了消防员的控制能力”。周五两场独立的野火合并成为一场大火，几乎与邻近的卡斯蒂利亚莱昂地区的另一场大火合并。总理佩德罗·桑切斯原定于周六上午在火区中心的塞尼森托斯村庄参加紧急计划会议，并在随后接受媒体采访。在法国，当局周六从郊区疏散了数千人波尔多附近地区的野火没有减弱的迹象。负责波尔多地区的新阿基坦和吉伦特省当地政府负责人索菲·布罗卡斯表示，勒海朗、艾西讷和梅里尼亚克地区正在被清理。波尔多地区以其葡萄园而闻名，该市是前往附近度假的游客的主要交通枢纽之一大约 44,000 人逃离了波尔多以南的高档费雷角半岛，唯一的道路受到火焰威胁。船只将数百人从大火中转移出来，其他人则驶离了以百万富翁住宅而闻名的半岛。那里有 50 多所房屋被毁。法国总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔努表示，迄今为止，吉伦特省和朗德地区已有超过 141,000 人被疏散。勒科尔努周六在 X 上写道：“袭击我们国家的大火已经达到了前所未有的程度。”法国军队也已被征召前来提供帮助，而马克龙则已向欧盟寻求帮助。法国和西班牙官员称，法国西南部已有141,000人被疏散，马德里地区有25,000人被疏散，其中有1,200多名老年人和残疾人。自5月份以来，欧洲一些地区至少遭受了两次热浪。世界天气归因组织在本周发表的一项研究中表示，由于人类造成的气候变化而导致的干旱加剧了今年野火的威胁。

articles.title: How Jimothy the raccoon became the internet's latest animal obsession
articles.summary: It all began with an innocuous video shared by Seattle resident Kiana Hall on Instagram.
articles.titleZh: 浣熊吉莫西如何成为互联网上最新的动物迷
articles.summaryZh: 这一切都始于西雅图居民 Kiana Hall 在 Instagram 上分享的一段无伤大雅的视频。

contentParagraphs.en: How Jimothy the raccoon became the internet's latest animal obsessionFigure caption, Watch: Woman describes seeing Jimothy, the viral raccoon from SeattleByLiv McMahon and Laura CressTechnology reportersCharli XCX might be hoping the release of her new album sets off another Brat summer, but many believe the season has already been claimed by a furrier force - Jimothy.First spotted bounding across streets in Washington, the Seattle raccoon with an unusual, spindly shape and the scamper of a Tasmanian Devil has been seized on by the internet as a new hit meme.Like Moo Deng and Neil the Seal before him, he is the latest cute, distinctive and seemingly chaotic creature to be immortalised in amateur footage, sometimes cringeworthy brand posts, and even murals.But what is it about Jimothy, as he's been nicknamed, that has gripped the internet?It all began with an innocuous video shared by Seattle resident Kiana Hall on Instagram."What am I looking at?" Hall could be heard exclaiming, as the unusual-looking raccoon hurtles across a pavement and up some nearby steps.A caption alongside it referred to the creature as "Jimothy the raccoon with short spine syndrome".While it is not known for sure if the condition has caused his appearance, many have assumed as such, and the description has stuck.Image source, Instagram/Kiana HallAs Hall's Instagram reel spread, it attracted more and more likes, comments and reposts, with more than eight million views as of Friday morning."My brother was talking about Jimothy the other day, and I asked him who he is," reads one comment on Hall's video. "He told me Jimothy would find me, and now he has."Some users have also praised the raccoon's online fame for drawing attention to spine conditions."I hope that someone can care for Jimothy as a wild animal... he will get older and need more care," wrote one user, who said she had been born with a congenital spine syndrome.Jimothy would not be the first to attract online fame for such a condition, Australian YouTuber Lessons in Meme Culture points out, external.A dog called Pig became a brief internet sensation in 2014 owing in part to having short spine syndrome.Why is he everywhere?In a strange pop cultural tradition that covers the likes of Doge and Grumpy Cat, Jimothy has found himself in the crosshairs of media attention for being two things - an unusual animal and very shareable."As cities expand and food waste increases, humans and raccoons cross paths more often," said digital culture researcher Dr Idil Galip."More encounters mean more footage of raccoons being funny and in today's fast-moving, saturated feeds, that footage can become a meme almost instantly."He hasn't just been celebrated in posts from fans across social media.The online outpouring of love for Jimothy has also since translated into the real world - with one local artist celebrating him with a mural in the neighbourhood of Ballard, where he was first spotted.This Instagram post cannot be displayed in your browser. Please enable Javascript or try a different browser.View original content on InstagramThe BBC is not responsible for the content of external sites.Skip instagram postAllow Instagram content?This article contains content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. You may want to read Meta’s Instagram cookie policy, external and privacy policy, external before accepting. To view this content choose ‘accept and continue’.The BBC is not responsible for the content of external sites.President Donald Trump's White House social media accounts, no stranger to tapping into online culture to promote his agenda, have also shared a Jimothy meme.In a post on X, external, it portrayed the raccoon donning a red hat emblazoned with "Trump was right about everything".Blissfully unaware of his 15 seconds of viral fame, the raccoon has become fodder for brands racing to capitalise on consumer interest in the latest online trend.Among the things Jimothy has amassed so far are:A Google animation which runs across the screen when you search "Jimothy"Meme coins named in his honour - part of a grand tradition where crypto fans jump on viral moments to make digital coins with questionable valueAn upcoming appearance, external in World of Warcraft's fictional Azeroth"Meme marketing is now standard practice for many brands," said Dr Galip."They will hop on to whatever's trending, hoping the visibility rubs off on them. "A viral moment can give momentary brand visibility, in searches and social media feeds, where the attention is."He's even popped up in Minecraft, or so the official account claims.From naughty penguins to ungovernable elephant seals, funny animals attracting attention on the internet is nothing new.But the surge of interest and drive to document these quirky, characterful creatures can often result in pleas from local officials to respect their privacy and safety.People in Washington and its most populous city Seattle have been similarly warned not to approach Jimothy to protect him and themselves."As long as you don't try to pet him, cuddle him or feed him, Jimothy poses zero public health risk," said the state health department on Threads, external.Figure caption, But in an otherwise overwhelming online landscape, some feel these viral moments offer some relief."The internet is a lot. It is too much, constantly, in every direction," writes Jamie Slack on her blog, Totally the Bomb, external."And then Jimothy shows up and for one brief weird moment everyone is on the same page - rooting for this little gremlin, giggling at his name, feeling weirdly connected to strangers over absolutely nothing."
contentParagraphs.zh: 浣熊吉莫西 (Jimothy) 如何成为互联网上最新的动物迷。图标题，观看：女人描述看到来自西雅图的病毒浣熊吉莫西 (Jimothy) 作者：Liv McMahon 和 Laura Cress 科技记者 Charli XCX 可能希望她的新专辑的发行会引发又一个 Brat 夏天，但许多人认为这个季节已经被毛皮势力 - 吉莫西 (Jimothy) 占领了。 西雅图浣熊首次被发现在华盛顿的街道上跳跃，它的形状不寻常，细长塔斯马尼亚恶魔的奔跑行为已成为互联网上的新热门模因。就像 Moo Deng 和 Neil the Seal 一样，他是最新的可爱、独特且看似混乱的生物，在业余镜头、有时令人尴尬的品牌帖子、甚至壁画中永垂不朽。但是，吉莫西（他的昵称）是如何引起互联网关注的呢？这一切都始于西雅图居民 Kiana Hall 分享的一段无伤大雅的视频。在 Instagram 上。“我在看什么？”当这只长相不寻常的浣熊冲过人行道并爬上附近的一些台阶时，可以听到霍尔的惊呼声。旁边的说明文字将这种生物称为“患有短脊柱综合症的浣熊吉莫西”。虽然不确定这种情况是否导致了它的出现，但许多人都这么认为，并且描述已经固定下来。图片来源，Instagram/Kiana Hall随着霍尔的 Instagram 视频传播，它吸引了越来越多的点赞、评论和转发，超过截至周五早上，观看次数已达 800 万次。“有一天，我哥哥在谈论吉莫西，我问他是谁，”霍尔视频上的一条评论写道。 “他告诉我吉莫西会找到我，现在他找到了。”一些用户还赞扬了浣熊在网上的名气，因为它引起了人们对脊柱状况的关注。“我希望有人能像照顾野生动物一样照顾吉莫西……他会变老，需要更多的照顾，”一位用户写道，她说她天生患有先天性脊柱综合症。澳大利亚 YouTuber Lessons in Meme Culture 指出，吉莫西不会是第一个因这种情况而在网上成名的人。猪在 2014 年在网络上短暂走红，部分原因是患有短脊柱综合症。为什么他无处不在？在一种奇怪的流行文化传统中，包括狗狗和脾气暴躁的猫，吉莫西发现自己因为两件事而成为媒体关注的焦点：一种不寻常的动物和非常善于分享。“随着城市的扩张和食物浪费的增加，人类和浣熊交叉的频率越来越高，”数字文化研究员伊迪尔·加利普博士说。“更多的相遇意味着更多的浣熊镜头。有趣的是，在当今快速发展、饱和的信息流中，这段视频几乎可以立即成为模因。“他不仅仅在社交媒体上的粉丝帖子中受到庆祝。网上对吉莫西的爱也转化为现实世界 - articles.title: UK mortgage rates rise to highest level for a month
articles.summary: Renewed tensions in the Middle East feed through to the costs faced by lenders, pushing up borrowing costs.
articles.titleZh: 英国抵押贷款利率升至一个月来最高水平
articles.summaryZh: 中东重新出现的紧张局势加剧了贷款机构面临的成本，推高了借贷成本。

contentParagraphs.en: Image source, Getty ImagesByCost of living correspondentUpdated 20 minutes agoUK average mortgage rates have risen back to the level of a month ago as renewed tensions in the Middle East feed through to homeowners.Lenders' funding costs have increased as markets judge that a prolonged conflict reduces the possibility of interest rate cuts by central banks. The five biggest High Street banks are among a host of lenders which have increased their interest rates on new fixed deals in recent days.Recent projections by the Bank of England suggest just over five million homeowners should expect their monthly mortgage repayments to increase by the end of 2028.Mortgage rates had been falling as a ceasefire between the US and Iran initially appeared to hold.But fresh strikes and Houthi militia attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea reignited fears over global energy supplies.Oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May on Thursday after several days of increases, stoking fears of higher inflation and a lower likelihood of interest rate cuts.Average rate still below Iran war peakMore than eight in 10 mortgage customers have fixed-rate deals.The interest rate on this kind of mortgage does not change until the deal expires, usually after two or five years, and a new one is chosen to replace it.The average rate on a new two-year fixed deal is 5.59%, according to financial information service Moneyfacts. Although it has risen consistently in recent days and is the highest since 19 June, it remains below the Iran war peak in April of 5.9%.The average rate on a five-year fixed deal is 5.61%, a level last seen on 7 June.HSBC has also announced it will raise its mortgage rates on Monday."It will be incredibly frustrating for borrowers to see rates rise back up to where they were a month ago. The positive progress over recent weeks now feels all but lost, but what the market needs is a period of stability," said Rachel Springall, finance expert at Moneyfacts.She said 100 deals had been pulled temporarily as lenders reconsider their pricing plans.She suggested that anyone who needed to remortgage this year could lock in a new deal now with their existing lender ahead of time, but should also seek help from a broker to see whether there are better deals elsewhere. "Brokers are an anchor during turbulent times as they can help borrowers keep abreast of changes and be there step by step when going through a mortgage application," she said.Borrowers had been heartened by the regular falls in mortgage rates during June and early July, but brokers say the latest changes are evidence of the uncertainty in the sector."Any borrower hoping for rate cuts to become an ongoing trend will need to rethink," said David Hollingworth, of L&C Mortgages."Momentum has performed an about turn and now clearly shifted to fixed rates rising in the near term at least."Get our flagship newsletter with all the headlines you need to start the day. articles.title: Video: Scientists watch orcas ram a sunfish so hard it explodes
articles.summary: Marine biologists off of Baja California recorded one orca teeing up another to smash a sunfish into pieces. Scientists say there could be a reason for this behavior — or it could be just for entertainment.
articles.titleZh: 视频：科学家观察虎鲸猛烈撞击翻车鱼导致爆炸
articles.summaryZh: 下加利福尼亚州的海洋生物学家记录到，一只逆戟鲸与另一只逆戟鲸将翻车鱼撕成碎片。科学家表示，这种行为可能是有原因的，也可能只是为了娱乐。

contentParagraphs.en: Orcas are known for surprising behaviors. A new study documents two cases of orcas ramming sunfish so hard that the fish explode.
contentParagraphs.zh: 虎鲸以令人惊讶的行为而闻名。一项新的研究记录了两起逆戟鲸撞击太阳鱼致使鱼爆炸的案例。

contentParagraphs.en: NurPhoto/Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: NurPhoto/Getty Images

contentParagraphs.en: NurPhoto/Getty Images
contentParagraphs.zh: NurPhoto/Getty Images

contentParagraphs.en: "Don't play with your food" is a rule orcas don't seem to follow.
contentParagraphs.zh: “不要玩弄食物”是虎鲸似乎不遵守的规则。

contentParagraphs.en: Off the shores of Cabo San Lucas, Kathryn Ayres, a scientist at the ocean-health nonprofit Beneath The Waves, saw a surprising orca behavior: One orca holds a sunfish in its mouth, while another lines up and then rams it at high speed — leaving behind thousands of sunfish bits scattered like confetti.
contentParagraphs.zh: 海洋健康非营利组织Beneath The Waves的科学家凯瑟琳·艾尔斯（ Kathryn Ayres ）在卡波圣卢卡斯（ Cabo San Lucas ）海岸外看到了一种令人惊讶的逆戟鲸行为：一只逆戟鲸嘴里含着太阳鱼，而另一只逆戟鲸排队，然后高速撞击它—留下成千上万的太阳鱼碎片像纸屑一样散落。

contentParagraphs.en: Ayres and her co-authors documented this "stabilize-and-ram" behavior in a paper published Thursday.
contentParagraphs.zh: 艾尔斯和她的合著者在周四发表的一篇论文中记录了这种“稳定和公羊”的行为。

contentParagraphs.en: "Seeing a large animal burst into fragments looks shocking," says study co-author Erick Higuera, a marine biologist at Conexiones Terramar.
contentParagraphs.zh: 研究合著者、Conexiones Terramar海洋生物学家埃里克·伊格拉（ Erick Higuera ）说： “看到一只大型动物爆裂成碎片看起来令人震惊。”

contentParagraphs.en: But "it isn't 'crazy' or 'cruel,'" he says, but rather "highly specialized biology."
contentParagraphs.zh: 但“这不是'疯狂'或'残酷' ，”他说，而是“高度专业化的生物学”。

contentParagraphs.en: "We think this may help younger orcas feed more easily — or it could also just be for fun," Ayres says. "Orcas are known for playing with their food."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们认为这可能有助于年轻的虎鲸更容易进食—或者也可能只是为了好玩，”艾尔斯说。“虎鲸以玩弄食物而闻名。”

contentParagraphs.en: In fact, these marine mammals have been documented displaying all kinds of "playful" behaviors. Orcas off of Washington state have been seen wearing salmon as hats. And some adolescent orcas take up a hobby of sinking ships.
contentParagraphs.zh: 事实上，这些海洋哺乳动物已被记录在案，表现出各种“好玩”的行为。有人看到华盛顿州的虎鲸戴着鲑鱼作为帽子。一些青少年虎鲸的爱好是沉船。

contentParagraphs.en: They're like cats, says Robert Pitman, a marine ecologist at Oregon State University who wasn't involved with the study. He says, like cats, orcas like to "torment prey and non-prey alike."
contentParagraphs.zh: 俄勒冈州立大学的海洋生态学家罗伯特·皮特曼（ Robert Pitman ）说，它们就像猫一样，没有参与这项研究。他说，像猫一样，逆戟鲸喜欢“折磨猎物和非猎物”。

contentParagraphs.en: But Pitman thinks this is primarily a feeding behavior. He notes some older orcas that eat sharks have trouble eating later in life due to teeth worn down to their gums — as do young orcas without teeth. Sunfish, like sharks, can be tough to eat. They can weigh thousands of pounds and have incredibly dense, rubbery, and collagenous skin several inches thick. And if that wasn't trouble enough, "there just doesn't seem to be much to eat on a sunfish," he says.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但Pitman认为这主要是一种进食行为。他指出，由于牙齿磨损到牙龈，一些吃鲨鱼的老虎鲸在以后的生活中难以进食—没有牙齿的年轻虎鲸也是如此。太阳鱼和鲨鱼一样，很难吃。它们可以重达数千磅，具有令人难以置信的致密、橡胶状和胶原质皮肤，厚达几英寸。如果这还不够麻烦， “在太阳鱼身上吃的东西似乎并不多，”他说。

contentParagraphs.en: "I think this behavior is a clever way to deal with a difficult prey item," he says. Given the context, the ramming behavior could be a more efficient method to eat sunfish than meticulously pulling it apart.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我认为这种行为是处理困难猎物的聪明方法，”他说。在这种情况下，撞击行为可能是吃太阳鱼的一种更有效的方法，而不是小心翼翼地将太阳鱼分开。

contentParagraphs.en: Higuera came to the same conclusion. "Orcas do not possess hands or tools to tear apart their prey," he says — so ramming sunfish to "bite-size pieces" is "incredibly practical."
contentParagraphs.zh: 伊格拉也得出了同样的结论。“虎鲸没有手或工具来撕裂猎物，”他说，因此将太阳鱼撞成“一口大小的碎片”是“非常实用的”。

contentParagraphs.en: Whether this behavior is "fun" is still an open question. For the behavior to be "fun," Higuera says, it needs to be voluntary, rewarding and involve modified or exaggerated behaviors. There are two documented cases of this behavior: one caught by Ayres in July 2024, and another filmed by a tourism operator last September. And in both examples, he notes it has aspects of being a social game like a sport, with one orca teeing up another to ram it. But he says it could also be a kind of parental care, with the adults preparing food for teething juveniles.

contentParagraphs.en: He says it is likely a feeding-plus-fun social activity, but would like to see more examples of this behavior before drawing any conclusions. For example, Higuera says if scientists saw adults doing it without toothless orcas present and not eating the shredded sunfish at all, that would support the case that it's simply entertainment.
contentParagraphs.zh: He says it is likely a feeding-plus-fun social activity, but would like to see more examples of this behavior before drawing any conclusions. For example, Higuera says if scientists saw adults doing it without toothless orcas present and not eating the shredded sunfish at all, that would support the case that it's simply entertainment.

contentParagraphs.en: While both of the documented cases took place in Baja California, Pitman says it remains to be seen whether other orcas around the world practice this "innovation" too. Higuera is also interested. He doesn't know if it was the same orcas involved in the two cases, but thinks it is likely a "cultural knowledge" restricted to a handful of pods in the area.

contentParagraphs.en: Pitman applauds the authors for elucidating this behavior. He says he's seen orcas carrying sunfish like "a large pizza box in its mouth" many times before and did not know what they were doing. "Maybe now I know," he says.

contentParagraphs.en: He warns, however, "for some snorkeling thrill seeker" hoping to see the orcas, that they should be careful not to end up as the pizza box themselves.
